summary: AI observability matters because LLM applications introduce unique failure modes—hallucinations, latency spikes, runaway token costs—that traditional APM tools were not designed to catch. As the LLM observability platform market grows from $2.69 billion in 2026 toward $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR, teams that invest in proper monitoring gain the ability to trace prompts end-to-end, attribute costs to users or departments, and evaluate output quality before problems reach production. Gartner predicts LLM observability investments will account for 50% of all GenAI deployments by 2028, up from just 15% in early 2026, signaling that this tooling is rapidly becoming non-negotiable.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain execution steps, agent loops, prompt versions, and evaluation runs across LangChain and non-LangChain applications
features: End-to-end trace visualization for chains and agents
Prompt versioning and A/B testing hub
Built-in human and automated evaluation workflows
Dataset management for regression testing
Overage-based trace metering with per-seat pricing
Integration with LangChain, LangGraph, and custom SDKs
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39/seat/month with overage ~$2.50 per 1,000 traces at standard retention; 100,000 traces on Plus costs approximately $264; Enterprise pricing available
tools.best_for: Teams already using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep chain-level debugging, prompt management, and structured evaluation pipelines

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests, token consumption, cost per request, latency, user-level spend, and model comparisons across 300+ supported models
features: Single base-URL proxy integration requiring one line of code change
Cost tracking across 300+ models via open-source model-cost repository
Department and user-level cost attribution and governance
Request caching to reduce redundant API spend
Prompt templates and experiment tracking
SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA compliance on Team tier and above
Open-source and fully self-hostable
tools.pricing: Hobby tier free at 10,000 requests/month; Pro at $79/month with unlimited seats and usage-based costs beyond included volume; Team at $799/month adding compliance certifications; custom Enterprise pricing with SAML SSO and on-prem options
tools.best_for: Teams that need instant cost visibility with minimal integration effort, especially for attributing spend by user, team, or product feature without restructuring existing code

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM calls, agent traces, evaluation metrics, experiment runs, model artifacts, and dataset versions within the broader W&B MLOps ecosystem
features: Unified tracing for LLM calls and multi-step agent workflows
Deep integration with W&B Experiments for comparing model runs
Built-in evaluation framework with custom and pre-built scorers
Dataset versioning and lineage tracking
Interactive dashboards for latency, cost, and quality metrics
Strong support for fine-tuning workflows alongside inference monitoring
tools.pricing: Free tier available for individuals; Team pricing varies by seat and usage; contact W&B for Enterprise pricing; consumption-based model for hosted artifact storage
tools.best_for: ML engineering teams that train, fine-tune, and deploy LLMs and want a single platform spanning the full model lifecycle from experiment to production observability

tools.name: Arize AI (Arize Phoenix)
tools.monitors: LLM traces, retrieval quality for RAG pipelines, embedding drift, model performance metrics, and long-standing ML model monitoring signals
features: Open-source Phoenix library for local and cloud tracing
RAG-specific evaluation including retrieval precision and context relevance
Embedding visualization and drift detection
Online and offline evaluation with RAGAS and custom evals
Extends traditional ML monitoring to LLM and multimodal workloads
OpenTelemetry-compatible instrumentation
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize cloud platform offers a free Developer tier; paid tiers scale by data volume and seats; Enterprise pricing on request
tools.best_for: Teams running RAG applications or migrating from traditional ML monitoring who need strong retrieval evaluation and embedding-level diagnostics alongside standard LLM tracing

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt versions, token usage, cost, latency, and evaluation scores across any LLM provider or framework
features: Open-source with MIT license and full self-hosting support
Detailed nested trace and span visualization
Prompt management with versioning and production rollout controls
Native evaluation integrations including DeepEval and custom scorers
Cost tracking across multiple providers with user and session attribution
SDKs for Python, JavaScript, and OpenTelemetry-based auto-instrumentation
Active open-source community and rapid feature cadence
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and self-hostable at no cost; Langfuse Cloud offers a free Hobby tier; Pro and Team cloud tiers available with usage-based pricing; Enterprise cloud and on-prem pricing on request
tools.best_for: Developer teams and startups that want a fully open-source, framework-agnostic observability platform with strong prompt management and the flexibility to self-host for data privacy

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM API calls, vector database queries, framework orchestration steps, token counts, and latency via OpenTelemetry-native instrumentation across any provider
features: OpenTelemetry-native: emits standard OTLP traces compatible with any backend
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and more
Drop-in integration requiring minimal code changes
Vendor-agnostic: send data to Datadog, Honeycomb, Grafana, Langfuse, or any OTLP collector
Open-source under Apache 2.0 license
Spans for vector store operations including Pinecone, Weaviate, and Chroma
tools.pricing: Fully open-source and free; costs depend only on the observability backend you route data to
tools.best_for: Platform and infrastructure teams that want vendor-agnostic LLM instrumentation using existing OpenTelemetry pipelines without adopting a proprietary SDK or new SaaS platform

cost_tips: Implement prompt caching and request deduplication: tools like Helicone offer built-in caching so identical or near-identical prompts return stored responses without hitting the LLM API, which can reduce redundant spend by 20–40% for applications with repetitive query patterns

Use observability data to right-size your model selection: trace-level cost breakdowns in tools like Langfuse or Helicone reveal which tasks consume the most tokens, enabling you to route simpler subtasks to smaller, cheaper models while reserving frontier models only for high-complexity requests

Set user- and team-level spend budgets and rate limits: platforms like Helicone and LangSmith support cost attribution by user session or department, allowing you to enforce hard caps before a single runaway agent loop or misconfigured batch job generates unexpected five-figure API bills

Audit and trim prompt bloat through prompt versioning: prompt management features in LangSmith and Langfuse let you A/B test shorter prompt variants against quality metrics, as unnecessary system prompt verbosity and redundant few-shot examples often account for 15–30% of token spend with no measurable quality benefit
